units.right_text: And as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder.

units.left_text: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain. The LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
units.right_text: The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the summit. So Moses went up,

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
units.right_text: and the LORD said to him, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish.

units.left_text: Let the priests also, who come near to the LORD, sanctify themselves, lest the LORD break out on them.”
units.right_text: Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them.”

units.left_text: Moses said to the LORD, “The people can’t come up to Mount Sinai, for you warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the mountain, and sanctify it.’”
units.right_text: But Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’”

units.left_text: The LORD said to him, “Go down! You shall bring Aaron up with you, but don’t let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest he break out against them.”
units.right_text: And the LORD replied, “Go down and bring Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break out against them.”

units.left_text: So Moses went down to the people, and told them.
units.right_text: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

units.left_text: God spoke all these words, saying,
units.right_text: And God spoke all these words:

units.left_text: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
units.right_text: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

units.left_text: “You shall have no other gods before me.
units.right_text: You shall have no other gods before Me.

units.left_text: “You shall not make for yourselves an idol, nor any image of anything that is in the heavens above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:
units.right_text: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.

units.left_text: you shall not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me,
units.right_text: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,

units.left_text: and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
units.right_text: but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.

units.left_text: “You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not hold him guiltless who misuses his name.
units.right_text: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.

units.left_text: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
units.right_text: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

units.left_text: You shall labor six days, and do all your work,
units.right_text: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

units.left_text: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
units.right_text: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work— neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates.

units.left_text: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
units.right_text: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.

units.left_text: “Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
units.right_text: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

units.left_text: “You shall not murder.
units.right_text: You shall not murder.

units.left_text: “You shall not commit adultery.
units.right_text: You shall not commit adultery.

units.left_text: “You shall not steal.
units.right_text: You shall not steal.

units.left_text: “You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
units.right_text: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

units.left_text: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
units.right_text: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”

units.left_text: All the people perceived the thunderings, the lightnings, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking. When the people saw it, they trembled, and stayed at a distance.
units.right_text: When all the people witnessed the thunder and lightning, the sounding of the ram’s horn, and the mountain enveloped in smoke, they trembled and stood at a distance.

units.left_text: They said to Moses, “Speak with us yourself, and we will listen; but don’t let God speak with us, lest we die.”
units.right_text: “Speak to us yourself and we will listen,” they said to Moses. “But do not let God speak to us, or we will die.”

units.left_text: Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid, for God has come to test you, and that his fear may be before you, that you won’t sin.”
units.right_text: “Do not be afraid,” Moses replied. “For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.”

units.left_text: The people stayed at a distance, and Moses came near to the thick darkness where God was.
units.right_text: And the people stood at a distance as Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “This is what you shall tell the children of Israel: ‘You yourselves have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is what you are to tell the Israelites: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.

units.left_text: You shall most certainly not make gods of silver or gods of gold for yourselves to be alongside me.
units.right_text: You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.

units.left_text: You shall make an altar of earth for me, and shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I record my name I will come to you and I will bless you.
units.right_text: You are to make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and cattle. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.

units.left_text: If you make me an altar of stone, you shall not build it of cut stones; for if you lift up your tool on it, you have polluted it.
units.right_text: Now if you make an altar of stones for Me, you must not build it with stones shaped by tools; for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.

units.left_text: You shall not go up by steps to my altar, that your nakedness may not be exposed to it.’
units.right_text: And you must not go up to My altar on steps, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’[’’]

units.left_text: “Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before them:
units.right_text: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:

units.left_text: “If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go out free without paying anything.
units.right_text: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.

units.left_text: If he comes in by himself, he shall go out by himself. If he is married, then his wife shall go out with him.
units.right_text: If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.

units.left_text: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.
units.right_text: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.

units.left_text: But if the servant shall plainly say, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children. I will not go out free;’
units.right_text: But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’

units.left_text: then his master shall bring him to God, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.
units.right_text: then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.

units.left_text: “If a man sells his daughter to be a female servant, she shall not go out as the male servants do.
units.right_text: And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.

units.left_text: If she doesn’t please her master, who has married her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt deceitfully with her.
units.right_text: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.

units.left_text: If he marries her to his son, he shall deal with her as a daughter.
units.right_text: And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.

units.left_text: If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.
units.right_text: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.

units.left_text: If he doesn’t do these three things for her, she may go free without paying any money.
units.right_text: If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment.

units.left_text: “One who strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death,
units.right_text: Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.

units.left_text: but not if it is unintentional, but God allows it to happen; then I will appoint you a place where he shall flee.
units.right_text: If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.

units.left_text: If a man schemes and comes presumptuously on his neighbor to kill him, you shall take him from my altar, that he may die.
units.right_text: But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.

units.left_text: “Anyone who attacks his father or his mother shall be surely put to death.
units.right_text: Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.

units.left_text: “Anyone who kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
units.right_text: Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.

units.left_text: “Anyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
units.right_text: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.

units.left_text: “If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone, or with his fist, and he doesn’t die, but is confined to bed;
units.right_text: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,

units.left_text: if he rises again and walks around with his staff, then he who struck him shall be cleared; only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is thoroughly healed.
units.right_text: then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.

units.left_text: “If a man strikes his servant or his maid with a rod, and he dies under his hand, the man shall surely be punished.
units.right_text: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.

units.left_text: Notwithstanding, if his servant gets up after a day or two, he shall not be punished, for the servant is his property.
units.right_text: However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.

units.left_text: “If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the woman’s husband demands and the judges allow.
units.right_text: If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.

units.left_text: But if any harm follows, then you must take life for life,
units.right_text: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life —

units.left_text: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
units.right_text: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

units.left_text: burning for burning, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.
units.right_text: burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.

units.left_text: “If a man strikes his servant’s eye, or his maid’s eye, and destroys it, he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.
units.right_text: If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.

units.left_text: If he strikes out his male servant’s tooth, or his female servant’s tooth, he shall let the servant go free for his tooth’s sake.
units.right_text: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.

units.left_text: “If a bull gores a man or a woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.
units.right_text: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.

units.left_text: But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and this has been testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.
units.right_text: But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.

units.left_text: If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed.
units.right_text: If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.

units.left_text: Whether it has gored a son or has gored a daughter, according to this judgment it shall be done to him.
units.right_text: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.

units.left_text: If the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, thirty shekels of silver shall be given to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.
units.right_text: If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.

units.left_text: “If a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and doesn’t cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it,
units.right_text: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,

units.left_text: the owner of the pit shall make it good. He shall give money to its owner, and the dead animal shall be his.
units.right_text: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.

units.left_text: “If one man’s bull injures another’s, so that it dies, then they shall sell the live bull, and divide its price; and they shall also divide the dead animal.
units.right_text: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.

units.left_text: Or if it is known that the bull was in the habit of goring in the past, and its owner has not kept it in, he shall surely pay bull for bull, and the dead animal shall be his own.
units.right_text: But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.[’’]

units.left_text: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
units.right_text: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.

units.left_text: If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt of bloodshed for him.
units.right_text: If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.

units.left_text: If the sun has risen on him, he is guilty of bloodshed. He shall make restitution. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
units.right_text: But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed.

units.left_text: If the stolen property is found in his hand alive, whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall pay double.
units.right_text: If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession— whether ox or donkey or sheep— he must pay back double.

units.left_text: “If a man causes a field or vineyard to be eaten by letting his animal loose, and it grazes in another man’s field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field, and from the best of his own vineyard.
units.right_text: If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.

units.left_text: “If fire breaks out, and catches in thorns so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
units.right_text: If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.

units.left_text: “If a man delivers to his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it is stolen out of the man’s house, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
units.right_text: If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.

units.left_text: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.
units.right_text: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.

units.left_text: For every matter of trespass, whether it is for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, or for any kind of lost thing, about which one says, ‘This is mine,’ the cause of both parties shall come before God. He whom God condemns shall pay double to his neighbor.
units.right_text: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.

units.left_text: “If a man delivers to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies or is injured, or driven away, no man seeing it;
units.right_text: If a man gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to be cared for by his neighbor, but it dies or is injured or stolen while no one is watching,

units.left_text: the oath of the LORD shall be between them both, he has not put his hand on his neighbor’s goods; and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.
units.right_text: an oath before the LORD shall be made between the parties to determine whether or not the man has taken his neighbor’s property. The owner must accept the oath and require no restitution.

units.left_text: But if it is stolen from him, the one who stole shall make restitution to its owner.
units.right_text: But if the animal was actually stolen from the neighbor, he must make restitution to the owner.

units.left_text: If it is torn in pieces, let him bring it for evidence. He shall not make good that which was torn.
units.right_text: If the animal was torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for the torn carcass.

units.left_text: “If a man borrows anything of his neighbor’s, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make restitution.
units.right_text: If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.

units.left_text: If its owner is with it, he shall not make it good. If it is a leased thing, it came for its lease.
units.right_text: If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss.

units.left_text: “If a man entices a virgin who isn’t pledged to be married, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife.
units.right_text: If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and sleeps with her, he must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.

units.left_text: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
units.right_text: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man still must pay an amount comparable to the bridal price of a virgin.

units.left_text: “You shall not allow a sorceress to live.
units.right_text: You must not allow a sorceress to live.

units.left_text: “Whoever has sex with an animal shall surely be put to death.
units.right_text: Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death.

units.left_text: “He who sacrifices to any god, except to the LORD only, shall be utterly destroyed.
units.right_text: If anyone sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone, he must be set apart for destruction.

units.left_text: “You shall not wrong an alien or oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
units.right_text: You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

units.left_text: “You shall not take advantage of any widow or fatherless child.
units.right_text: You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.

units.left_text: If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry;
units.right_text: If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.

units.left_text: and my wrath will grow hot, and I will kill you with the sword; and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
units.right_text: My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless.

units.left_text: “If you lend money to any of my people with you who is poor, you shall not be to him as a creditor. You shall not charge him interest.
units.right_text: If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.

units.left_text: If you take your neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
units.right_text: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,

units.left_text: for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What would he sleep in? It will happen, when he cries to me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.
units.right_text: because his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.

units.left_text: “You shall not blaspheme God, nor curse a ruler of your people.
units.right_text: You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.

units.left_text: “You shall not delay to offer from your harvest and from the outflow of your presses.
units.right_text: You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.

units.left_text: You shall do likewise with your cattle and with your sheep. It shall be with its mother seven days, then on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
units.right_text: You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.

units.left_text: “You shall be holy men to me, therefore you shall not eat any meat that is torn by animals in the field. You shall cast it to the dogs.
units.right_text: You are to be My holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.[’’]

units.left_text: “You shall not spread a false report. Don’t join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
units.right_text: “You shall not spread a false report. Do not join the wicked by being a malicious witness.

units.left_text: “You shall not follow a crowd to do evil. You shall not testify in court to side with a multitude to pervert justice.
units.right_text: You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.

units.left_text: You shall not favor a poor man in his cause.
units.right_text: And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.

units.left_text: “If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again.
units.right_text: If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.

units.left_text: If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.
units.right_text: If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.

units.left_text: “You shall not deny justice to your poor people in their lawsuits.
units.right_text: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.

units.left_text: “Keep far from a false charge, and don’t kill the innocent and righteous; for I will not justify the wicked.
units.right_text: Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.

units.left_text: “You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.
units.right_text: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.

units.left_text: “You shall not oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
units.right_text: Do not oppress a foreign resident, since you yourselves know how it feels to be foreigners; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

units.left_text: “For six years you shall sow your land, and shall gather in its increase,
units.right_text: For six years you are to sow your land and gather its produce,

units.left_text: but the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the poor of your people may eat; and what they leave the animal of the field shall eat. In the same way, you shall deal with your vineyard and with your olive grove.
units.right_text: but in the seventh year you must let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove.

units.left_text: “Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your servant, and the alien may be refreshed.
units.right_text: For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.

units.left_text: “Be careful to do all things that I have said to you; and don’t invoke the name of other gods or even let them be heard out of your mouth.
units.right_text: Pay close attention to everything I have said to you. You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.

units.left_text: “You shall observe a feast to me three times a year.
units.right_text: Three times a year you are to celebrate a feast to Me.

units.left_text: You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it you came out of Egypt), and no one shall appear before me empty.
units.right_text: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread as I commanded you: At the appointed time in the month of Abib you are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, because that was the month you came out of Egypt. No one may appear before Me empty-handed.

units.left_text: And the feast of harvest, the first fruits of your labors, which you sow in the field; and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when you gather in your labors out of the field.
units.right_text: You are also to keep the Feast of Harvest with the firstfruits of the produce from what you sow in the field.

units.left_text: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord GOD.
units.right_text: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.

units.left_text: “You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. The fat of my feast shall not remain all night until the morning.
units.right_text: You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened, nor may the fat of My feast remain until morning.

units.left_text: You shall bring the first of the first fruits of your ground into the house of the LORD your God.
units.right_text: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.

units.left_text: “Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
units.right_text: Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.

units.left_text: Pay attention to him, and listen to his voice. Don’t provoke him, for he will not pardon your disobedience, for my name is in him.
units.right_text: Pay attention to him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive rebellion, since My Name is in him.

units.left_text: But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries.
units.right_text: But if you will listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.

units.left_text: For my angel shall go before you, and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I will cut them off.
units.right_text: For My angel will go before you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will annihilate them.

units.left_text: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor follow their practices, but you shall utterly overthrow them and demolish their pillars.
units.right_text: You must not bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their practices. Instead, you are to demolish them and smash their sacred stones to pieces.

units.left_text: You shall serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will take sickness away from among you.
units.right_text: So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. And I will take away sickness from among you.

units.left_text: No one will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fulfill the number of your days.
units.right_text: No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren; I will fulfill the number of your days.

units.left_text: I will send my terror before you, and will confuse all the people to whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
units.right_text: I will send My terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn and run.

units.left_text: I will send the hornet before you, which will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before you.
units.right_text: I will send the hornet before you to drive the Hivites and Canaanites and Hittites out of your way.

units.left_text: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the animals of the field multiply against you.
units.right_text: I will not drive them out before you in a single year; otherwise the land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply against you.

units.left_text: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.
units.right_text: Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you become fruitful and possess the land.

units.left_text: I will set your border from the Red Sea even to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.
units.right_text: And I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. For I will deliver the inhabitants into your hand, and you will drive them out before you.

units.left_text: You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
units.right_text: You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.

units.left_text: They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against me, for if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”
units.right_text: They must not remain in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me. For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”

units.left_text: He said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD, you, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and worship from a distance.
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD — you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders — and you are to worship at a distance.

units.left_text: Moses alone shall come near to the LORD, but they shall not come near. The people shall not go up with him.”
units.right_text: Moses alone shall approach the LORD, but the others must not come near. And the people may not go up with him.”

units.left_text: Moses came and told the people all the LORD’s words, and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, and said, “All the words which the LORD has spoken will we do.”
units.right_text: When Moses came and told the people all the words and ordinances of the LORD, they all responded with one voice: “All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do.”

units.left_text: Moses wrote all the LORD’s words, then rose up early in the morning and built an altar at the base of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
units.right_text: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD.

units.left_text: He sent young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings of cattle to the LORD.
units.right_text: Then he sent out some young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.

units.left_text: Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
units.right_text: Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he splattered on the altar.

units.left_text: He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people, and they said, “We will do all that the LORD has said, and be obedient.”
units.right_text: Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it to the people, who replied, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient.”

units.left_text: Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which the LORD has made with you concerning all these words.”
units.right_text: So Moses took the blood, splattered it on the people, and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.”

units.left_text: Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
units.right_text: Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel,

units.left_text: They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the skies for clearness.
units.right_text: and they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet was a work like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.

units.left_text: He didn’t lay his hand on the nobles of the children of Israel. They saw God, and ate and drank.
units.right_text: But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank.

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain, and stay here, and I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands that I have written, that you may teach them.”
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and stay here, so that I may give you the tablets of stone, with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.”

units.left_text: Moses rose up with Joshua, his servant, and Moses went up onto God’s Mountain.
units.right_text: So Moses set out with Joshua his attendant and went up on the mountain of God.

units.left_text: He said to the elders, “Wait here for us, until we come again to you. Behold, Aaron and Hur are with you. Whoever is involved in a dispute can go to them.”
units.right_text: And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.”

units.left_text: Moses went up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
units.right_text: When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it,

units.left_text: The LORD’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he called to Moses out of the middle of the cloud.
units.right_text: and the glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered it, and on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud.

units.left_text: The appearance of the LORD’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel.
units.right_text: And the sight of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop in the eyes of the Israelites.

units.left_text: Moses entered into the middle of the cloud, and went up on the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
units.right_text: Moses entered the cloud as he went up on the mountain, and he remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “Speak to the children of Israel, that they take an offering for me. From everyone whose heart makes him willing you shall take my offering.
units.right_text: “Tell the Israelites to bring Me an offering. You are to receive My offering from every man whose heart compels him.

units.left_text: This is the offering which you shall take from them: gold, silver, bronze,
units.right_text: This is the offering you are to accept from them:

units.left_text: blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
units.right_text: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn;

units.left_text: rams’ skins dyed red, sea cow hides, acacia wood,
units.right_text: ram skins dyed red and fine leather;

units.left_text: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense,
units.right_text: olive oil for the light;

units.left_text: onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
units.right_text: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.

units.left_text: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.
units.right_text: And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them.

units.left_text: According to all that I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all of its furniture, even so you shall make it.
units.right_text: You must make the tabernacle and design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you.

units.left_text: “They shall make an ark of acacia wood. Its length shall be two and a half cubits, its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
units.right_text: And they are to construct an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.

units.left_text: You shall overlay it with pure gold. You shall overlay it inside and outside, and you shall make a gold molding around it.
units.right_text: Overlay it with pure gold both inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.

units.left_text: You shall cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in its four feet. Two rings shall be on the one side of it, and two rings on the other side of it.
units.right_text: Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.

units.left_text: You shall make poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
units.right_text: And make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

units.left_text: You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
units.right_text: Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, in order to carry it.

units.left_text: The poles shall be in the rings of the ark. They shall not be taken from it.
units.right_text: The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark; they must not be removed.

units.left_text: You shall put the covenant which I shall give you into the ark.
units.right_text: And place inside the ark the Testimony, which I will give you.

units.left_text: You shall make a mercy seat of pure gold. Two and a half cubits shall be its length, and a cubit and a half its width.
units.right_text: And you are to construct a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

units.left_text: You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat.
units.right_text: Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,

units.left_text: Make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim on its two ends of one piece with the mercy seat.
units.right_text: one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.

units.left_text: The cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces toward one another. The faces of the cherubim shall be toward the mercy seat.
units.right_text: And the cherubim are to have wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat. The cherubim are to face each other, looking toward the mercy seat.

units.left_text: You shall put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and in the ark you shall put the covenant that I will give you.
units.right_text: Set the mercy seat atop the ark and put the Testimony that I will give you into the ark.

units.left_text: There I will meet with you, and I will tell you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the covenant, all that I command you for the children of Israel.
units.right_text: And I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony; I will speak with you about all that I command you regarding the Israelites.

units.left_text: “You shall make a table of acacia wood. Its length shall be two cubits, and its width a cubit, and its height one and a half cubits.
units.right_text: You are also to make a table of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.

units.left_text: You shall overlay it with pure gold, and make a gold molding around it.
units.right_text: Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.

units.left_text: You shall make a rim of a hand width around it. You shall make a golden molding on its rim around it.
units.right_text: And make a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.

units.left_text: You shall make four rings of gold for it, and put the rings in the four corners that are on its four feet.
units.right_text: Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners at its four legs.

units.left_text: The rings shall be close to the rim, for places for the poles to carry the table.
units.right_text: The rings are to be close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.

units.left_text: You shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold, that the table may be carried with them.
units.right_text: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, so that the table may be carried with them.

units.left_text: You shall make its dishes, its spoons, its ladles, and its bowls with which to pour out offerings. You shall make them of pure gold.
units.right_text: You are also to make the plates and dishes, as well as the pitchers and bowls for pouring drink offerings. Make them out of pure gold.

units.left_text: You shall set bread of the presence on the table before me always.
units.right_text: And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times.

units.left_text: “You shall make a lamp stand of pure gold. The lamp stand shall be made of hammered work. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its flowers shall be of one piece with it.
units.right_text: Then you are to make a lampstand of pure, hammered gold. It shall be made of one piece, including its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals.

units.left_text: There shall be six branches going out of its sides: three branches of the lamp stand out of its one side, and three branches of the lamp stand out of its other side;
units.right_text: Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand — three on one side and three on the other.

units.left_text: three cups made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower; and three cups made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower, so for the six branches going out of the lamp stand;
units.right_text: There are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extend from the lampstand.

units.left_text: and in the lamp stand four cups made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;
units.right_text: And on the lampstand there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms with buds and petals.

units.left_text: and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, and a bud under two branches of one piece with it, for the six branches going out of the lamp stand.
units.right_text: For the six branches that extend from the lampstand, a bud must be under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.

units.left_text: Their buds and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it one beaten work of pure gold.
units.right_text: The buds and branches are to be all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.

units.left_text: You shall make its lamps seven, and they shall light its lamps to give light to the space in front of it.
units.right_text: Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it.

units.left_text: Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of pure gold.
units.right_text: The wick trimmers and their trays must be of pure gold.

units.left_text: It shall be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these accessories.
units.right_text: The lampstand and all these utensils shall be made from a talent of pure gold.

units.left_text: See that you make them after their pattern, which has been shown to you on the mountain.
units.right_text: See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain. [’’]

units.left_text: “Moreover you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim. You shall make them with the work of a skillful workman.
units.right_text: “You are to construct the tabernacle itself with ten curtains of finely spun linen, each with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and cherubim skillfully worked into them.

units.left_text: The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains shall have one measure.
units.right_text: Each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide — all curtains the same size.

units.left_text: Five curtains shall be coupled together to one another, and the other five curtains shall be coupled to one another.
units.right_text: Five of the curtains are to be joined together, and the other five joined as well.

units.left_text: You shall make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling, and you shall do likewise on the edge of the curtain that is outermost in the second coupling.
units.right_text: Make loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same for the end curtain in the second set.

units.left_text: You shall make fifty loops in the one curtain, and you shall make fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling. The loops shall be opposite one another.
units.right_text: Make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops line up opposite one another.

units.left_text: You shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains to one another with the clasps. The tabernacle shall be a unit.
units.right_text: Make fifty gold clasps as well, and join the curtains together with the clasps, so that the tabernacle will be a unit.

units.left_text: “You shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
units.right_text: You are to make curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle — eleven curtains in all.

units.left_text: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits: the eleven curtains shall have one measure.
units.right_text: Each of the eleven curtains is to be the same size — thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.

units.left_text: You shall couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shall double over the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tent.
units.right_text: Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another. Then fold the sixth curtain over double at the front of the tent.

units.left_text: You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outermost in the coupling, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which is outermost in the second coupling.
units.right_text: Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.

units.left_text: You shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
units.right_text: Make fifty bronze clasps and put them through the loops to join the tent together as a unit.

units.left_text: The overhanging part that remains of the curtains of the tent—the half curtain that remains—shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.
units.right_text: As for the overlap that remains of the tent curtains, the half curtain that is left over shall hang down over the back of the tabernacle.

units.left_text: The cubit on the one side and the cubit on the other side, of that which remains in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
units.right_text: And the tent curtains will be a cubit longer on either side, and the excess will hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it.

units.left_text: You shall make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sea cow hides above.
units.right_text: Also make a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.

units.left_text: “You shall make the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
units.right_text: You are to construct upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.

units.left_text: Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and one and a half cubits the width of each board.
units.right_text: Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

units.left_text: There shall be two tenons in each board, joined to one another: thus you shall make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
units.right_text: Two tenons must be connected to each other for each frame. Make all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.

units.left_text: You shall make twenty boards for the tabernacle, for the south side southward.
units.right_text: Construct twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle,

units.left_text: You shall make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.
units.right_text: with forty silver bases under the twenty frames — two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.

units.left_text: For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, twenty boards,
units.right_text: For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames

units.left_text: and their forty sockets of silver; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
units.right_text: and forty silver bases — two bases under each frame.

units.left_text: For the far side of the tabernacle westward you shall make six boards.
units.right_text: Make six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the west side,

units.left_text: You shall make two boards for the corners of the tabernacle in the far side.
units.right_text: and two frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle,

units.left_text: They shall be double beneath, and in the same way they shall be whole to its top to one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.
units.right_text: coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring. These will serve as the two corners.

units.left_text: There shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.
units.right_text: So there are to be eight frames and sixteen silver bases — two under each frame.

units.left_text: “You shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
units.right_text: You are also to make five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,

units.left_text: and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the far side westward.
units.right_text: five for those on the other side, and five for those on the rear side of the tabernacle, to the west.

units.left_text: The middle bar in the middle of the boards shall pass through from end to end.
units.right_text: The central crossbar in the middle of the frames shall extend from one end to the other.

units.left_text: You shall overlay the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold for places for the bars. You shall overlay the bars with gold.
units.right_text: Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars with gold.

units.left_text: You shall set up the tabernacle according to the way that it was shown to you on the mountain.
units.right_text: So you are to set up the tabernacle according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.

units.left_text: “You shall make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cherubim. It shall be the work of a skillful workman.
units.right_text: Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.

units.left_text: You shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, on four sockets of silver.
units.right_text: Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood, overlaid with gold and standing on four silver bases.

units.left_text: You shall hang up the veil under the clasps, and shall bring the ark of the covenant in there within the veil. The veil shall separate the holy place from the most holy for you.
units.right_text: And hang the veil from the clasps and place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil. So the veil will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

units.left_text: You shall put the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant in the most holy place.
units.right_text: Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.

units.left_text: You shall set the table outside the veil, and the lamp stand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south. You shall put the table on the north side.
units.right_text: And place the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and put the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side.

units.left_text: “You shall make a screen for the door of the Tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer.
units.right_text: For the entrance to the tent, you are to make a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.

units.left_text: You shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia, and overlay them with gold. Their hooks shall be of gold. You shall cast five sockets of bronze for them.
units.right_text: Make five posts of acacia wood for the curtain, overlay them with gold, use hooks of gold, and cast five bronze bases for them.[’’]

units.left_text: “You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long, and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square. Its height shall be three cubits.
units.right_text: “You are to build an altar of acacia wood. The altar must be square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.

units.left_text: You shall make its horns on its four corners. Its horns shall be of one piece with it. You shall overlay it with bronze.
units.right_text: Make a horn on each of its four corners, so that the horns are of one piece, and overlay it with bronze.

units.left_text: You shall make its pots to take away its ashes; and its shovels, its basins, its meat hooks, and its fire pans. You shall make all its vessels of bronze.
units.right_text: Make all its utensils of bronze — its pots for removing ashes, its shovels, its sprinkling bowls, its meat forks, and its firepans.

units.left_text: You shall make a grating for it of network of bronze. On the net you shall make four bronze rings in its four corners.
units.right_text: Construct for it a grate of bronze mesh, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the mesh.

units.left_text: You shall put it under the ledge around the altar beneath, that the net may reach halfway up the altar.
units.right_text: Set the grate beneath the ledge of the altar, so that the mesh comes halfway up the altar.

units.left_text: You shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
units.right_text: Additionally, make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.

units.left_text: Its poles shall be put into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when carrying it.
units.right_text: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on two sides of the altar when it is carried.

units.left_text: You shall make it hollow with planks. They shall make it as it has been shown you on the mountain.
units.right_text: Construct the altar with boards so that it is hollow. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.

units.left_text: “You shall make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen one hundred cubits long for one side.
units.right_text: You are also to make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side of the courtyard make curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on one side,

units.left_text: Its pillars shall be twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze. The hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.
units.right_text: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.

units.left_text: Likewise for the length of the north side, there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, and its pillars twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
units.right_text: Likewise there are to be curtains on the north side, a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.

units.left_text: For the width of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
units.right_text: The curtains on the west side of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide, with ten posts and ten bases.

units.left_text: The width of the court on the east side eastward shall be fifty cubits.
units.right_text: The east side of the courtyard, toward the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits wide.

units.left_text: The hangings for the one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
units.right_text: Make the curtains on one side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,

units.left_text: For the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
units.right_text: and the curtains on the other side fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.

units.left_text: For the gate of the court shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer; their pillars four, and their sockets four.
units.right_text: The gate of the courtyard shall be twenty cubits long, with a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It shall have four posts and four bases.

units.left_text: All the pillars of the court around shall be filleted with silver; their hooks of silver, and their sockets of bronze.
units.right_text: All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.

units.left_text: The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, and the width fifty throughout, and the height five cubits, of fine twined linen, and their sockets of bronze.
units.right_text: The entire courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely spun linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.

units.left_text: All the instruments of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its pins, and all the pins of the court, shall be of bronze.
units.right_text: All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, including all its tent pegs and the tent pegs of the courtyard, shall be made of bronze.

units.left_text: “You shall command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.
units.right_text: And you are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.

units.left_text: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the covenant, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before the LORD: it shall be a statute forever throughout their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.
units.right_text: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come.[’’]

units.left_text: “Bring Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, near to you from among the children of Israel, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.
units.right_text: “Next, have your brother Aaron brought to you from among the Israelites, along with his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, to serve Me as priests.

units.left_text: You shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
units.right_text: Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, to give him glory and splendor.

units.left_text: You shall speak to all who are wise-hearted, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
units.right_text: You are to instruct all the skilled craftsmen, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, to make garments for Aaron’s consecration, so that he may serve Me as priest.

units.left_text: These are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and his sons, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
units.right_text: These are the garments that they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may serve Me as priests.

units.left_text: They shall use the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen.
units.right_text: They shall use gold, along with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.

units.left_text: “They shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the skillful workman.
units.right_text: They are to make the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, and with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.

units.left_text: It shall have two shoulder straps joined to the two ends of it, that it may be joined together.
units.right_text: It shall have two shoulder pieces attached at two of its corners, so it can be fastened.

units.left_text: The skillfully woven band, which is on it, shall be like its work and of the same piece; of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen.
units.right_text: And the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod must be of one piece, of the same workmanship — with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.

units.left_text: You shall take two onyx stones, and engrave on them the names of the children of Israel.
units.right_text: Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:

units.left_text: Six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six that remain on the other stone, in the order of their birth.
units.right_text: six of their names on one stone and the remaining six on the other, in the order of their birth.

units.left_text: With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones, according to the names of the children of Israel. You shall make them to be enclosed in settings of gold.
units.right_text: Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount the stones in gold filigree settings.

units.left_text: You shall put the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel. Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD on his two shoulders for a memorial.
units.right_text: Fasten both stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel. Aaron is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD.

units.left_text: You shall make settings of gold,
units.right_text: Fashion gold filigree settings

units.left_text: and two chains of pure gold; you shall make them like cords of braided work. You shall put the braided chains on the settings.
units.right_text: and two chains of pure gold, made of braided cord work; and attach these chains to the settings.

units.left_text: “You shall make a breastplate of judgment, the work of the skillful workman; like the work of the ephod you shall make it; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, you shall make it.
units.right_text: You are also to make a breastpiece of judgment with the same workmanship as the ephod. Construct it with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.

units.left_text: It shall be square and folded double; a span shall be its length, and a span its width.
units.right_text: It must be square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide.

units.left_text: You shall set in it settings of stones, four rows of stones: a row of ruby, topaz, and beryl shall be the first row;
units.right_text: And mount on it a setting of gemstones, four rows of stones:

units.left_text: and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald;
units.right_text: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;

units.left_text: and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
units.right_text: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;

units.left_text: and the fourth row a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They shall be enclosed in gold in their settings.
units.right_text: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper.

units.left_text: The stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
units.right_text: The twelve stones are to correspond to the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.

units.left_text: You shall make on the breastplate chains like cords, of braided work of pure gold.
units.right_text: For the breastpiece, make braided chains like cords of pure gold.

units.left_text: You shall make on the breastplate two rings of gold, and shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
units.right_text: You are also to make two gold rings and fasten them to the two corners of the breastpiece.

units.left_text: You shall put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.
units.right_text: Then fasten the two gold chains to the two gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,

units.left_text: The other two ends of the two braided chains you shall put on the two settings, and put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod in its forepart.
units.right_text: and fasten the other ends of the two chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.

units.left_text: You shall make two rings of gold, and you shall put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge, which is toward the side of the ephod inward.
units.right_text: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.

units.left_text: You shall make two rings of gold, and shall put them on the two shoulder straps of the ephod underneath, in its forepart, close by its coupling, above the skillfully woven band of the ephod.
units.right_text: Make two additional gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near its seam just above its woven waistband.

units.left_text: They shall bind the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate may not swing out from the ephod.
units.right_text: The rings of the breastpiece shall be tied to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece is above the waistband of the ephod and does not swing out from the ephod.

units.left_text: Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment on his heart, when he goes in to the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually.
units.right_text: Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he shall bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment, as a continual reminder before the LORD.

units.left_text: You shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be on Aaron’s heart, when he goes in before the LORD. Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel on his heart before the LORD continually.
units.right_text: And place the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so that they will also be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before the LORD. Aaron will continually carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the LORD.

units.left_text: “You shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
units.right_text: You are to make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,

units.left_text: It shall have a hole for the head in the middle of it. It shall have a binding of woven work around its hole, as it were the hole of a coat of mail, that it not be torn.
units.right_text: with an opening at its top in the center. Around the opening shall be a woven collar with an opening like that of a garment, so that it will not tear.

units.left_text: On its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, all around its hem; with bells of gold between and around them:
units.right_text: Make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn all the way around the lower hem, with gold bells between them,

units.left_text: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.
units.right_text: alternating the gold bells and pomegranates around the lower hem of the robe.

units.left_text: It shall be on Aaron to minister: and its sound shall be heard when he goes in to the holy place before the LORD, and when he comes out, that he not die.
units.right_text: Aaron must wear the robe whenever he ministers, and its sound will be heard when he enters or exits the sanctuary before the LORD, so that he will not die.

units.left_text: “You shall make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, like the engravings of a signet, ‘HOLY TO THE LORD.’
units.right_text: You are to make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it as on a seal:

units.left_text: You shall put it on a lace of blue, and it shall be on the sash. It shall be on the front of the sash.
units.right_text: Fasten to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.

units.left_text: It shall be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things, which the children of Israel shall make holy in all their holy gifts; and it shall be always on his forehead, that they may be accepted before the LORD.
units.right_text: And it will be worn on Aaron’s forehead, so that he may bear the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate with regard to all their holy gifts. It shall always be on his forehead, so that they may be acceptable before the LORD.

units.left_text: You shall weave the tunic with fine linen. You shall make a turban of fine linen. You shall make a sash, the work of the embroiderer.
units.right_text: You are to weave the tunic with fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and fashion an embroidered sash.

units.left_text: “You shall make tunics for Aaron’s sons. You shall make sashes for them. You shall make headbands for them, for glory and for beauty.
units.right_text: Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron’s sons, to give them glory and splendor.

units.left_text: You shall put them on Aaron your brother, and on his sons with him, and shall anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister to me in the priest’s office.
units.right_text: After you put these garments on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests.

units.left_text: You shall make them linen pants to cover their naked flesh. They shall reach from the waist even to the thighs.
units.right_text: Make linen undergarments to cover their bare flesh, extending from waist to thigh.

units.left_text: They shall be on Aaron and on his sons, when they go in to the Tent of Meeting, or when they come near to the altar to minister in the holy place, that they don’t bear iniquity, and die. This shall be a statute forever to him and to his offspring after him.
units.right_text: Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they will not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants.[’’]
