units.left_text: “This is the thing that you shall do to them to make them holy, to minister to me in the priest’s office: take one young bull and two rams without defect,
units.right_text: “Now this is what you are to do to consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests: Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,

units.left_text: unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. You shall make them of fine wheat flour.
units.right_text: along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil. Make them out of fine wheat flour,

units.left_text: You shall put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, with the bull and the two rams.
units.right_text: put them in a basket, and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.

units.left_text: You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall wash them with water.
units.right_text: Then present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.

units.left_text: You shall take the garments, and put on Aaron the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, and clothe him with the skillfully woven band of the ephod.
units.right_text: Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastplate. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.

units.left_text: You shall set the turban on his head, and put the holy crown on the turban.
units.right_text: Put the turban on his head and attach the holy diadem to the turban.

units.left_text: Then you shall take the anointing oil, and pour it on his head, and anoint him.
units.right_text: Then take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head.

units.left_text: You shall bring his sons, and put tunics on them.
units.right_text: Present his sons as well and clothe them with tunics.

units.left_text: You shall clothe them with belts, Aaron and his sons, and bind headbands on them. They shall have the priesthood by a perpetual statute. You shall consecrate Aaron and his sons.
units.right_text: Wrap the sashes around Aaron and his sons and tie headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons.

units.left_text: “You shall bring the bull before the Tent of Meeting; and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.
units.right_text: You are to present the bull at the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.

units.left_text: You shall kill the bull before the LORD at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: And you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: You shall take of the blood of the bull, and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; and you shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
units.right_text: Take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger; then pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

units.left_text: You shall take all the fat that covers the innards, the cover of the liver, the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, and burn them on the altar.
units.right_text: Take all the fat that covers the entrails and the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.

units.left_text: But the meat of the bull, and its skin, and its dung, you shall burn with fire outside of the camp. It is a sin offering.
units.right_text: But burn the flesh of the bull and its hide and dung outside the camp; it is a sin offering.

units.left_text: “You shall also take the one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
units.right_text: Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.

units.left_text: You shall kill the ram, and you shall take its blood, and sprinkle it around on the altar.
units.right_text: You are to slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splatter it on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: You shall cut the ram into its pieces, and wash its innards, and its legs, and put them with its pieces, and with its head.
units.right_text: Cut the ram into pieces, wash the entrails and legs, and place them with its head and other pieces.

units.left_text: You shall burn the whole ram on the altar: it is a burnt offering to the LORD; it is a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.right_text: Then burn the entire ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.

units.left_text: “You shall take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
units.right_text: Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head.

units.left_text: Then you shall kill the ram, and take some of its blood, and put it on the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and on the tip of the right ear of his sons, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot; and sprinkle the blood around on the altar.
units.right_text: Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Splatter the remaining blood on all sides of the altar.

units.left_text: You shall take of the blood that is on the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron, and on his garments, and on his sons, and on the garments of his sons with him: and he shall be made holy, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments with him.
units.right_text: And take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments will be consecrated, as well as his sons and their garments.

units.left_text: Also you shall take some of the ram’s fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the innards, the cover of the liver, the two kidneys, the fat that is on them, and the right thigh (for it is a ram of consecration),
units.right_text: Take the fat from the ram, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, both kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh (since this is a ram for ordination),

units.left_text: and one loaf of bread, one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer out of the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
units.right_text: along with one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.

units.left_text: You shall put all of this in Aaron’s hands, and in his sons’ hands, and shall wave them for a wave offering before the LORD.
units.right_text: Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering.

units.left_text: You shall take them from their hands, and burn them on the altar on the burnt offering, for a pleasant aroma before the LORD: it is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
units.right_text: Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar atop the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is a food offering to the LORD.

units.left_text: “You shall take the breast of Aaron’s ram of consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before the LORD. It shall be your portion.
units.right_text: Take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s ordination and wave it before the LORD as a wave offering, and it will be your portion.

units.left_text: You shall sanctify the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the wave offering, which is waved, and which is raised up, of the ram of consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons.
units.right_text: Consecrate for Aaron and his sons the breast of the wave offering that is waved and the thigh of the heave offering that is lifted up from the ram of ordination.

units.left_text: It shall be for Aaron and his sons as their portion forever from the children of Israel; for it is a wave offering. It shall be a wave offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifices of their peace offerings, even their wave offering to the LORD.
units.right_text: This will belong to Aaron and his sons as a regular portion from the Israelites, for it is the heave offering the Israelites will make to the LORD from their peace offerings.

units.left_text: “The holy garments of Aaron shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them, and to be consecrated in them.
units.right_text: The holy garments that belong to Aaron will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them.

units.left_text: Seven days shall the son who is priest in his place put them on, when he comes into the Tent of Meeting to minister in the holy place.
units.right_text: The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place must wear them for seven days.

units.left_text: “You shall take the ram of consecration and boil its meat in a holy place.
units.right_text: You are to take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.

units.left_text: Aaron and his sons shall eat the meat of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.

units.left_text: They shall eat those things with which atonement was made, to consecrate and sanctify them; but a stranger shall not eat of it, because they are holy.
units.right_text: They must eat those things by which atonement was made for their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because these things are sacred.

units.left_text: If anything of the meat of the consecration, or of the bread, remains to the morning, then you shall burn the remainder with fire. It shall not be eaten, because it is holy.
units.right_text: And if any of the meat of ordination or any bread is left until the morning, you are to burn up the remainder. It must not be eaten, because it is sacred.

units.left_text: “You shall do so to Aaron and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded you. You shall consecrate them seven days.
units.right_text: This is what you are to do for Aaron and his sons based on all that I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them.

units.left_text: Every day you shall offer the bull of sin offering for atonement. You shall cleanse the altar when you make atonement for it. You shall anoint it, to sanctify it.
units.right_text: Sacrifice a bull as a sin offering each day for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.

units.left_text: Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar, and sanctify it; and the altar shall be most holy. Whatever touches the altar shall be holy.
units.right_text: For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will become most holy; whatever touches the altar will be holy.

units.left_text: “Now this is that which you shall offer on the altar: two lambs a year old day by day continually.
units.right_text: This is what you are to offer regularly on the altar, each day: two lambs that are a year old.

units.left_text: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning; and the other lamb you shall offer at evening;
units.right_text: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.

units.left_text: and with the one lamb a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil, and the fourth part of a hin of wine for a drink offering.

units.right_text: Take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting. It will serve as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD to make atonement for your lives.”

units.right_text: Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Anyone who profanes it must surely be put to death. Whoever does any work on that day must be cut off from among his people.

units.right_text: For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day must surely be put to death.

units.right_text: When the LORD had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God.

units.left_text: Aaron said to them, “Take off the golden rings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them to me.”
units.right_text: So Aaron told them, “Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me.”

units.left_text: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made a proclamation, and said, “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.”
units.right_text: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: “Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD.”

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, “Go, get down; for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves!
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go down at once, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.

units.left_text: They have turned away quickly out of the way which I commanded them. They have made themselves a molded calf, and have worshiped it, and have sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your gods, Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.’”

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “I have seen these people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people.
units.right_text: The LORD also said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.

units.left_text: Now therefore leave me alone, that my wrath may burn hot against them, and that I may consume them; and I will make of you a great nation.”
units.right_text: Now leave Me alone, so that My anger may burn against them and consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation.”

units.left_text: Moses begged the LORD his God, and said, “LORD, why does your wrath burn hot against your people, that you have brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?
units.right_text: But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God, saying, “O LORD, why does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

units.left_text: Why should the Egyptians talk, saying, ‘He brought them out for evil, to kill them in the mountains, and to consume them from the surface of the earth’? Turn from your fierce wrath, and turn away from this evil against your people.

units.left_text: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by your own self, and said to them, ‘I will multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they shall inherit it forever.’”

units.left_text: So the LORD turned away from the evil which he said he would do to his people.

units.right_text: So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, let him take it off,’ and they gave it to me. And when I threw it into the fire, out came this calf!”

units.right_text: Afterward, Moses said, “Today you have been ordained for service to the LORD, since each man went against his son and his brother; so the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day.”

units.right_text: The next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”

units.right_text: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Oh, what a great sin these people have committed! They have made gods of gold for themselves.

units.right_text: Yet now, if You would only forgive their sin.... But if not, please blot me out of the book that You have written.”

units.right_text: Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you. But on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.”

units.right_text: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people; otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.”

units.left_text: The children of Israel stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.
units.right_text: So the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

units.left_text: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he called it “The Tent of Meeting.” Everyone who sought the LORD went out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.
units.right_text: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it at a distance outside the camp. He called it the Tent of Meeting, and anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.

units.left_text: When Moses went out to the Tent, all the people rose up, and stood, everyone at their tent door, and watched Moses, until he had gone into the Tent.
units.right_text: Then, whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would stand at the entrances to their own tents and watch Moses until he entered the tent.

units.left_text: When Moses entered into the Tent, the pillar of cloud descended, stood at the door of the Tent, and the LORD spoke with Moses.
units.right_text: As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.

units.left_text: All the people saw the pillar of cloud stand at the door of the Tent, and all the people rose up and worshiped, everyone at their tent door.
units.right_text: When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
units.right_text: Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.

units.left_text: Moses said to the LORD, “Behold, you tell me, ‘Bring up this people;’ and you haven’t let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’
units.right_text: Then Moses said to the LORD, “Look, You have been telling me, ‘Lead this people up,’ but You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in My sight.’

units.left_text: Now therefore, if I have found favor in your sight, please show me your way, now, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in your sight; and consider that this nation is your people.”
units.right_text: Now if indeed I have found favor in Your sight, please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight. Remember that this nation is Your people.”

units.left_text: He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
units.right_text: And the LORD answered, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”

units.left_text: Moses said to him, “If your presence doesn’t go with me, don’t carry us up from here.
units.right_text: “If Your Presence does not go with us,” Moses replied, “do not lead us up from here.

units.left_text: For how would people know that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Isn’t it that you go with us, so that we are separated, I and your people, from all the people who are on the surface of the earth?”
units.right_text: For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us? How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?”

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “I will do this thing also that you have spoken; for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
units.right_text: So the LORD said to Moses, “I will do this very thing you have asked, for you have found favor in My sight, and I know you by name.”

units.left_text: Moses said, “Please show me your glory.”
units.right_text: Then Moses said, “Please show me Your glory.”

units.left_text: He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim the LORD’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”
units.right_text: “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you,” the LORD replied, “and I will proclaim My name — the LORD — in your presence. I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”

units.left_text: He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
units.right_text: But He added, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.”

units.left_text: The LORD also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock.
units.right_text: The LORD continued, “There is a place near Me where you are to stand upon a rock,

units.left_text: It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and will cover you with my hand until I have passed by;
units.right_text: and when My glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.

units.left_text: then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back; but my face shall not be seen.”
units.right_text: Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.”

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “Chisel two stone tablets like the first. I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.

units.left_text: Be ready by the morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and present yourself there to me on the top of the mountain.
units.right_text: Be ready in the morning, and come up on Mount Sinai to present yourself before Me on the mountaintop.

units.left_text: No one shall come up with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. Do not let the flocks or herds graze in front of that mountain.”
units.right_text: No one may go up with you; in fact, no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain — not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of the mountain.”

units.left_text: He chiseled two tablets of stone like the first; then Moses rose up early in the morning, and went up to Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand two stone tablets.
units.right_text: So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the originals. He rose early in the morning, and taking the two stone tablets in his hands, he went up Mount Sinai as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: The LORD descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the LORD’s name.
units.right_text: And the LORD descended in a cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed His name, the LORD.

units.left_text: The LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
units.right_text: Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out:

units.left_text: keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
units.right_text: maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations,

units.left_text: Moses hurried and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshiped.
units.right_text: Moses immediately bowed down to the ground and worshiped.

units.left_text: He said, “If now I have found favor in your sight, Lord, please let the Lord go among us, even though this is a stiff-necked people; pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance.”
units.right_text: “O Lord,” he said, “if I have indeed found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.”

units.left_text: He said, “Behold, I make a covenant: before all your people I will do marvels, such as have not been worked in all the earth, nor in any nation; and all the people among whom you are shall see the work of the LORD; for it is an awesome thing that I do with you.
units.right_text: And the LORD said, “Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will perform wonders that have never been done in any nation in all the world. All the people among whom you live will see the LORD’s work, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.

units.left_text: Observe that which I command you today. Behold, I will drive out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
units.right_text: Observe what I command you this day. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

units.left_text: Be careful, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land where you are going, lest it be for a snare among you;
units.right_text: Be careful not to make a treaty with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest they become a snare in your midst.

units.left_text: but you shall break down their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and you shall cut down their Asherah poles;
units.right_text: Rather, you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.

units.left_text: for you shall worship no other god; for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
units.right_text: For you must not worship any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

units.left_text: “Don’t make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest they play the prostitute after their gods, and sacrifice to their gods, and one call you and you eat of his sacrifice;
units.right_text: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.

units.left_text: and you take of their daughters to your sons, and their daughters play the prostitute after their gods, and make your sons play the prostitute after their gods.
units.right_text: And when you take some of their daughters as brides for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and cause your sons to do the same.

units.left_text: “You shall make no cast idols for yourselves.
units.right_text: You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.

units.left_text: “You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib; for in the month Abib you came out of Egypt.
units.right_text: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, you are to eat unleavened bread as I commanded you. For in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.

units.left_text: “All that opens the womb is mine; and all your livestock that is male, the firstborn of cow and sheep.
units.right_text: The first offspring of every womb belongs to Me, including all the firstborn males among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep.

units.left_text: You shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb. If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck. You shall redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before me empty.
units.right_text: You must redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb; but if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.

units.left_text: “Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest: in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
units.right_text: Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in the seasons of plowing and harvesting, you must rest.

units.left_text: “You shall observe the feast of weeks with the first fruits of wheat harvest, and the feast of harvest at the year’s end.
units.right_text: And you are to celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.

units.left_text: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
units.right_text: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.

units.left_text: For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your borders; neither shall any man desire your land when you go up to appear before the LORD, your God, three times in the year.
units.right_text: For I will drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.

units.left_text: “You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. The sacrifice of the feast of the Passover shall not be left to the morning.
units.right_text: Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to Me along with anything leavened, and do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover Feast remain until morning.

units.left_text: “You shall bring the first of the first fruits of your ground to the house of the LORD your God.
units.right_text: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.

units.left_text: The LORD said to Moses, “Write these words; for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
units.right_text: The LORD also said to Moses, “Write down these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”

units.left_text: He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread, nor drank water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.
units.right_text: So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant — the Ten Commandments.

units.left_text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.
units.right_text: And when Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands, he was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.

units.left_text: When Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near him.
units.right_text: Aaron and all the Israelites looked at Moses, and behold, his face was radiant. And they were afraid to approach him.

units.left_text: Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them.
units.right_text: But Moses called out to them; so Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.

units.left_text: Afterward all the children of Israel came near, and he gave them all the commandments that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
units.right_text: And after this all the Israelites came near, and Moses commanded them to do everything that the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.

units.left_text: When Moses was done speaking with them, he put a veil on his face.
units.right_text: When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.

units.left_text: But when Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he took the veil off, until he came out; and he came out, and spoke to the children of Israel that which he was commanded.
units.right_text: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out. And when he came out, he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded,

units.left_text: The children of Israel saw Moses’ face, that the skin of Moses’ face shone; so Moses put the veil on his face again, until he went in to speak with him.
units.right_text: and the Israelites would see that the face of Moses was radiant. So Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.

units.left_text: Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said to them, “These are the words which the LORD has commanded, that you should do them.
units.right_text: Then Moses assembled the whole congregation of Israel and said to them, “These are the things that the LORD has commanded you to do:

units.left_text: ‘Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be a holy day for you, a Sabbath of solemn rest to the LORD: whoever does any work in it shall be put to death.
units.right_text: For six days work may be done, but the seventh day shall be your holy day, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Whoever does any work on that day must be put to death.

units.left_text: You shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations on the Sabbath day.’”
units.right_text: Do not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”

units.left_text: Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, “This is the thing which the LORD commanded, saying,
units.right_text: Moses also told the whole congregation of Israel, “This is what the LORD has commanded:

units.left_text: ‘Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it as the LORD’s offering: gold, silver, bronze,
units.right_text: Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring an offering to the LORD:

units.left_text: blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
units.right_text: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn;

units.left_text: rams’ skins dyed red, sea cow hides, acacia wood,
units.right_text: ram skins dyed red and fine leather;

units.left_text: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense,
units.right_text: olive oil for the light;

units.left_text: onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
units.right_text: and onyx stones and gemstones to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece.

units.left_text: “‘Let every wise-hearted man among you come, and make all that the LORD has commanded:
units.right_text: Let every skilled craftsman among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded:

units.left_text: the tabernacle, its outer covering, its roof, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
units.right_text: the tabernacle with its tent and covering, its clasps and frames, its crossbars, posts, and bases;

units.left_text: the ark, and its poles, the mercy seat, the veil of the screen;
units.right_text: the ark with its poles and mercy seat, and the veil to shield it;

units.left_text: the table with its poles and all its vessels, and the show bread;
units.right_text: the table with its poles, all its utensils, and the Bread of the Presence;

units.left_text: the lamp stand also for the light, with its vessels, its lamps, and the oil for the light;
units.right_text: the lampstand for light with its accessories and lamps and oil for the light;

units.left_text: and the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, the screen for the door, at the door of the tabernacle;
units.right_text: the altar of incense with its poles;

units.left_text: the altar of burnt offering, with its grating of bronze, its poles, and all its vessels, the basin and its base;
units.right_text: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils;

units.left_text: the hangings of the court, its pillars, their sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;
units.right_text: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, and the curtain for the gate of the courtyard;

units.left_text: the pins of the tabernacle, the pins of the court, and their cords;
units.right_text: the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard, along with their ropes;

units.left_text: the finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place—the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons—to minister in the priest’s office.’”
units.right_text: and the woven garments for ministering in the holy place— both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.”

units.left_text: All the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.
units.right_text: Then the whole congregation of Israel withdrew from the presence of Moses.

units.left_text: They came, everyone whose heart stirred him up, and everyone whom his spirit made willing, and brought the LORD’s offering for the work of the Tent of Meeting, and for all of its service, and for the holy garments.
units.right_text: And everyone whose heart stirred him and whose spirit prompted him came and brought an offering to the LORD for the work on the Tent of Meeting, for all its services, and for the holy garments.

units.left_text: They came, both men and women, as many as were willing-hearted, and brought brooches, earrings, signet rings, and armlets, all jewels of gold; even every man who offered an offering of gold to the LORD.
units.right_text: So all who had willing hearts, both men and women, came and brought brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry. And they all presented their gold as a wave offering to the LORD.

units.left_text: Everyone with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, and sea cow hides, brought them.
units.right_text: Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, or fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, or articles of fine leather, brought them.

units.left_text: Everyone who offered an offering of silver and bronze brought the LORD’s offering; and everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service, brought it.
units.right_text: And all who could present an offering of silver or bronze brought it as a contribution to the LORD. Also, everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the service brought it.

units.left_text: All the women who were wise-hearted spun with their hands, and brought that which they had spun: the blue, the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.
units.right_text: Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, or fine linen.

units.left_text: All the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun the goats’ hair.
units.right_text: And all the skilled women whose hearts were stirred spun the goat hair.

units.left_text: The rulers brought the onyx stones and the stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate;
units.right_text: The leaders brought onyx stones and gemstones to mount on the ephod and breastpiece,

units.left_text: with the spice and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the sweet incense.
units.right_text: as well as spices and olive oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.

units.left_text: The children of Israel brought a free will offering to the LORD; every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring for all the work, which the LORD had commanded to be made by Moses.
units.right_text: So all the men and women of the Israelites whose hearts prompted them brought a freewill offering to the LORD for all the work that the LORD through Moses had commanded them to do.

units.left_text: Moses said to the children of Israel, “Behold, the LORD has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
units.right_text: Then Moses said to the Israelites, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.

units.left_text: He has filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all kinds of workmanship;
units.right_text: And He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,

units.left_text: and to make skillful works, to work in gold, in silver, in bronze,
units.right_text: to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze,

units.left_text: in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of wood, to work in all kinds of skillful workmanship.
units.right_text: to cut gemstones for settings, and to carve wood, so that he may be a master of every artistic craft.

units.left_text: He has put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.
units.right_text: And the LORD has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.

units.left_text: He has filled them with wisdom of heart to work all kinds of workmanship, of the engraver, of the skillful workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of those who do any workmanship, and of those who make skillful works.
units.right_text: He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and as weavers — as artistic designers of every kind of craft.[’’]

units.left_text: “Bezalel and Oholiab shall work with every wise-hearted man, in whom the LORD has put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the LORD has commanded.”
units.right_text: “So Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person are to carry out everything commanded by the LORD, who has given them skill and ability to know how to perform all the work of constructing the sanctuary.”

units.left_text: Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even everyone whose heart stirred him up to come to the work to do it.
units.right_text: Then Moses summoned Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person whom the LORD had gifted — everyone whose heart stirred him to come and do the work.

units.left_text: They received from Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, with which to make it. They kept bringing free will offerings to him every morning.
units.right_text: They received from Moses all the contributions that the Israelites had brought to carry out the service of constructing the sanctuary.

units.left_text: All the wise men, who performed all the work of the sanctuary, each came from his work which he did.
units.right_text: so that all the skilled craftsmen who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left their work

units.left_text: They spoke to Moses, saying, “The people have brought much more than enough for the service of the work which the LORD commanded to make.”
units.right_text: and said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.”

units.left_text: Moses gave a commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman make anything else for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.
units.right_text: After Moses had given an order, they sent a proclamation throughout the camp: “No man or woman should make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing more,

units.left_text: For the stuff they had was sufficient to do all the work, and too much.
units.right_text: since what they already had was more than enough to perform all the work.

units.left_text: All the wise-hearted men among those who did the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim, the work of a skillful workman.
units.right_text: All the skilled craftsmen among the workmen made the ten curtains for the tabernacle. They were made of finely spun linen, as well as blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim skillfully worked into them.

units.left_text: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits. All the curtains had one measure.
units.right_text: Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains were the same size.

units.left_text: He coupled five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he coupled to one another.
units.right_text: And he joined five of the curtains together, and the other five he joined as well.

units.left_text: He made loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling. Likewise he made in the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the second coupling.
units.right_text: He made loops of blue material on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and also on the end curtain in the second set.

units.left_text: He made fifty loops in the one curtain, and he made fifty loops in the edge of the curtain that was in the second coupling. The loops were opposite to one another.
units.right_text: He made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops lined up opposite one another.

units.left_text: He made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains to one another with the clasps: so the tabernacle was a unit.
units.right_text: He also made fifty gold clasps to join the curtains together, so that the tabernacle was a unit.

units.left_text: He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle. He made them eleven curtains.
units.right_text: He then made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle — eleven curtains in all.

units.left_text: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and four cubits the width of each curtain. The eleven curtains had one measure.
units.right_text: Each of the eleven curtains was the same size — thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.

units.left_text: He coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
units.right_text: He joined five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another.

units.left_text: He made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was outermost in the coupling, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain which was outermost in the second coupling.
units.right_text: He made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the corresponding curtain in the second set.

units.left_text: He made fifty clasps of bronze to couple the tent together, that it might be a unit.
units.right_text: He also made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together as a unit.

units.left_text: He made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sea cow hides above.
units.right_text: Additionally, he made for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.

units.left_text: He made the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing up.

units.left_text: the pure lamp stand, its lamps, even the lamps to be set in order, all its vessels, the oil for the light,
units.right_text: the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its utensils, as well as the oil for the light;

units.left_text: the golden altar, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, the screen for the door of the Tent,
units.right_text: the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;

units.left_text: the bronze altar, its grating of bronze, its poles, all of its vessels, the basin and its base,
units.right_text: the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils;

units.left_text: the hangings of the court, its pillars, its sockets, the screen for the gate of the court, its cords, its pins, and all the instruments of the service of the tabernacle, for the Tent of Meeting,
units.right_text: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases;

units.left_text: the finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.
units.right_text: and the woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.

units.left_text: According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the work.
units.right_text: The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.left_text: Moses saw all the work, and behold, they had done it as the LORD had commanded. They had done so; and Moses blessed them.
units.right_text: And Moses inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.

units.left_text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
units.right_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

units.left_text: “On the first day of the first month you shall raise up the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: You shall put the ark of the covenant in it, and you shall screen the ark with the veil.
units.right_text: Put the ark of the Testimony in it and screen off the ark with the veil.

units.left_text: You shall bring in the table, and set in order the things that are on it. You shall bring in the lamp stand, and light its lamps.
units.right_text: Then bring in the table and set out its arrangement; bring in the lampstand as well, and set up its lamps.

units.left_text: You shall set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the covenant, and put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
units.right_text: Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the Testimony, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.

units.left_text: “You shall set the altar of burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.
units.right_text: Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.

units.left_text: You shall set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and shall put water therein.
units.right_text: And place the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.

units.left_text: You shall set up the court around it, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.
units.right_text: Set up the surrounding courtyard and hang the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard.

units.left_text: “You shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it, and shall make it holy, and all its furniture, and it will be holy.
units.right_text: Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it along with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.

units.left_text: You shall anoint the altar of burnt offering, with all its vessels, and sanctify the altar, and the altar will be most holy.
units.right_text: Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.

units.left_text: You shall anoint the basin and its base, and sanctify it.
units.right_text: Anoint the basin and its stand and consecrate them.

units.left_text: “You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and shall wash them with water.
units.right_text: Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.

units.left_text: You shall put on Aaron the holy garments; and you shall anoint him, and sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
units.right_text: And you are to clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as a priest.

units.left_text: You shall bring his sons, and put tunics on them.
units.right_text: Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.

units.left_text: You shall anoint them, as you anointed their father, that they may minister to me in the priest’s office. Their anointing shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”
units.right_text: Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may also serve Me as priests. Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.”

units.left_text: Moses did so. According to all that the LORD commanded him, so he did.
units.right_text: Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was raised up.
units.right_text: So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.

units.left_text: Moses raised up the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up its boards, and put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.
units.right_text: When Moses set up the tabernacle, he laid its bases, positioned its frames, inserted its crossbars, and set up its posts.

units.left_text: He spread the covering over the tent, and put the roof of the tabernacle above on it, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He took and put the covenant into the ark, and set the poles on the ark, and put the mercy seat above on the ark.
units.right_text: Moses took the Testimony and placed it in the ark, attaching the poles to the ark; and he set the mercy seat atop the ark.

units.left_text: He brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the covenant, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle, put up the veil for the screen, and shielded off the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside of the veil.
units.right_text: Moses placed the table in the Tent of Meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.

units.left_text: He set the bread in order on it before the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: He arranged the bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He put the lamp stand in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
units.right_text: He also placed the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle

units.left_text: He lit the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: and set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He put the golden altar in the Tent of Meeting before the veil;
units.right_text: Moses placed the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting, in front of the veil,

units.left_text: and he burned incense of sweet spices on it, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: and he burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He put up the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
units.right_text: Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.

units.left_text: He set the altar of burnt offering at the door of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the meal offering, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: He placed the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded him.

units.left_text: He set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water therein, with which to wash.
units.right_text: He placed the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing;

units.left_text: Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and their feet there.
units.right_text: and from it Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet.

units.left_text: When they went into the Tent of Meeting, and when they came near to the altar, they washed, as the LORD commanded Moses.
units.right_text: They washed whenever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

units.left_text: He raised up the court around the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.
units.right_text: And Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and he hung the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.

units.left_text: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the LORD’s glory filled the tabernacle.
units.right_text: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

units.left_text: Moses wasn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and the LORD’s glory filled the tabernacle.
units.right_text: Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

units.left_text: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward, throughout all their journeys;
units.right_text: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.

units.left_text: but if the cloud wasn’t taken up, then they didn’t travel until the day that it was taken up.
units.right_text: If the cloud was not lifted, they would not set out until the day it was taken up.

units.left_text: For the cloud of the LORD was on the tabernacle by day, and there was fire in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
units.right_text: For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.
